# Comparing the worlds

> *The same six questions have different answers for bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites, and the differences explain why each is detected, prevented and treated in its own way.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Compare the four kinds of microbe on each of the six questions; use the comparison to reason about an unfamiliar organism |
| The comparison | One table: six questions by four kinds of microbe, with an anchor organism in each column |
| Consequences | Why antibiotics do not treat viral infection; why antifungal and antiparasitic drugs are more toxic; why some infections can be prevented by vaccines and others by vector control |
| Scenario questions | Mixed questions across all four parts, interleaved, with the most likely kind of microbe as the first decision |
